nice! have you made any coils yet?

Not a single one. I have only used prebuilt coils for my Nautilus and my Subtank mini. I've seen a couple of videos of coil building, but never seen or done it in person.

Anything I should know?

wash your hands after nic absorbs through the skin. keep a good one handy so if you mess up a build you have one ready to go before you start feinding. ohm's readers are inexpensive and extremely helpful.

If you're going to do dual coils, wrap each one the same number of times, same spacing etc. You want them as close to identical as possible. Take your time with them, pulse fire to find "hot spots" and never touch the coils with anything metal when you're firing it. "Strumming" your coils while fine-tuning them will, for some reason, encourage them to glow evenly and from the middle. (This one defies logic, but it works.)

Cotton is cotton is cotton. Japanese cotton, "bacon" style cotton, organic cotton are all the same in my book. I prefer sheets of Japanese cotton, because it's much easier to use sharp scissors and cut lengths for wicks more accurately than pulling a clump off of a cotton ball and fiddling with it to get it even.

I mean, there's not much to it honestly - grab some wire, some tweezers, cotton and scissors, pop on a YouTube video (I personally like Rip, I know a lot of people don't, but the dude taught me how to roll coils) and follow along. The more you do, the better you'll get.

Don't crunch down on the leads until they break. That sucks, and means you'll likely have to scrap the whole coil and start over again. Snug, tight, but not so tight it cuts.

Don't worry about twisted this or clapton that yet, none of that matters in the beginning. All in due time. Just concentrate on getting decent, even wraps, get familiar with it, and you'll be off to the races in no time.
For how long the wicks should be, you want them to be touching the bottom of the deck without covering the whole thing. Make sure that the airflow is close to the coil.
